Episode 185: The Remaining People (1)
Twelve days had passed since the first day of July, 1803, the day the temporary alliance had their decisive battle with the evil spirits.
The world was regaining its old form.

The blue sky and the earth, unstained by chaos, the shining beach, the fishing boats sailing on the sea, the bustling marketplaces filled with people, and the everyday life that no longer needed to tremble in fear of evil spirits...
Thankfully.
Not only the Lutero Magic Federation and the Vermont Empire, but the entire continent had regained their familiar scenery.
Even the Hupester Alliance, which was once covered in chaos, was, to some extent, regaining its old appearance.
Not all the humans in Hupester had been used as sacrifices to the evil spirits.
When the chaos that had covered the entire continent had cleared, there were far more people remaining in Hupester than the temporary alliance had anticipated.

"Never knew that checking reports and numbers could be this delightful and fortunate. These numbers and words written on this paper, they're really the current status of survivors in each region, right?"
Mary said.
Although her face was extremely pale due to not having a good sleep since the end of the war, her eyes were sparkling brightly.
"Have you been fooled, sister! We and Tikan have been sending people to verify it directly. They are all real."
"So please, go inside and rest a little, get some sleep. We'll take care of the Rider duties. Stop asking the same question over and over."
The Tona brothers responded.
Their faces were also as pale as Mary's, but their eyes were bright.
"Are you guys trying to eat me alive just because I checked once or twice? Are you nuts?"
"Ha! Are you going to hit me? Go ahead!"
"Well, that's a bit, huh!"
Thump! Thump!
Mary left fist marks on the foreheads of the two.
"Ha! We, as Riders, have dignity too."
"I'm old enough. Ugh, my forehead."
"No one saw it. I'll let it slide because I'm in a good mood. Where's the youngest? Hasn't he woken up yet?"
"How many times are you asking about that...... Ah, put your fist down."
"Sister, you heard directly from the King about an hour ago. The youngest is recovering smoothly."
"I can't stop worrying because he hasn't regained consciousness."
"That's right. What was it? It wasn't that he was medically unconscious, but that he was just in a deep sleep. They emphasized that he will definitely wake up, so we don't need to worry."
"I understand you want to lessen any tasks when the youngest wakes up, but you'll hurt yourself more at this rate."
"Can you bring me the teapot?"
"Sigh."
The siblings didn't know.
From the moment they started talking, Jin had opened his eyes in another building.
There was no one in the room where Jin was lying because they had just gone to see off Lani.
For a while, Jin stared blankly at the ceiling.
'Where is this?'
A familiar yet unfamiliar ceiling, it wasn't Tikan's.
'...Sword Garden?'
The room he used when he was a trainee Rider.
It was there.
Even though Jin could move his body, he lay still, looking at the ceiling as if he were tied up.
He was afraid that it might not be a dream.
After Jin returned as a human, the Sword Garden had been destroyed several times.
Jin personally saw the destruction of the Sword Garden during the first total offensive, and the site where the giant evil spirit's castle was built was also where the Sword Garden used to be.
So he thought it was impossible for the Sword Garden to remain intact like this.
Jin calmed his trembling heart and looked back on his last memory.
He recalled the moment when he finished the fight with the evil spirit and fell to the ground.
'I think I saw the Sword Garden remaining intact then.'
He got up from his seat and pinched his arm.
It hurt. He pinched harder and even took a sip of water from the glass beside him.
The sensation of cold water flowing down his throat was clearer than ever.
"Master!"
Gilly's voice came.
"Jin!"
"12th Flagbearer!"
"Master!"
"Sir!"
"Jin!"
"Darling!"
Along with their voices were the voices of other comrades.
They all had just returned from seeing off the King.
Gilly suddenly hugged Jin, wiping away his tears.
The others also had moist eyes, especially Jet, who sat down crying, repeating over and over that 'Sir, sir, our sir has woken up.'
From the outside, hearing only Jet's crying, it might have been mistaken that Jin hadn't woken up but had died.
"Master, are you alright!"
"Honey! You don't have any pain, do you? Why have you been lying down for so long, do you know how much I've been hurting?"
"Jin, you've woken up in ten days. And as you can see... you did it. You saved the world, Runcandel. You have regained the Sword Garden."
At the moment when the comrades were saying various things, Jin felt a playful urge for some reason.
"...Who are you guys?"
"…Master?"
"And where is this place...?"
"What did you say?"
"Sir!?"
"Ji, Jin?"
"Honey? No, this can't be!"
The comrades widened their eyes in surprise, feeling their hearts sink.
Jin was going to add one more sentence, 'Who am I?' But Valeria came in, and his joke was exposed.
"You have a surprisingly naive side. Isn't it too much to play such a prank on those who have been anxiously waiting for you to wake up?"
Though her tone seemed reproachful, Valeria had a broad smile on her face.
She had been watching Jin's movements, keeping his record window open, except when he was sleeping for ten days.
The current record window showed Jin waking up from sleep and playing a prank.
"Did I go too far? I'm sorry, everyone."
"It was a lot, Master. I thought my heart was going to drop."
"I almost threw a punch."
"Honey, is your head really okay!?"
"Yeah, it's okay. I think my body needs some more recovery. Gilly, are all our comrades safe?"
"Yes, master. No one died in the Vamel Union."
The atmosphere seemed to suggest that. In this war, the Vamel Union had suffered the least damage.
No, beyond that, the Vamel Union had become much stronger than before the war.
Gilly and the comrades spent some time explaining the current situation to Jin.
Most of the allied clans and civilians of Huphester were safe, and in Runcandel, about three thousand knights, a hundred wizards, and numerous servants survived.
It's not entirely a happy situation.
The entire population of the city of Calon was used as a sacrifice, the number of knights who had died in corruption was countless, and globally, the number of deaths easily exceeded a million.
The disappeared ones don't come back, even though the monster is dead.
However, it was also true that the heart was overwhelmed with the fact that those things, which were thought to have all disappeared, were so left behind and giving off hope.
Those who survived had a basis for preparing for tomorrow.
That's why the comrades were excited all along.
They had to be excited, because only then they could push away the sorrow of war and move forward.

"The survival of this many people in Runcandel is the result of the monster's obsession with the clan to the end. The monster really wanted to leave the Sword Garden and Runcandel, even if it had to destroy the world."
Valeria opened the record window and confirmed the content.
It was the record of the monster's contradictory heart that even the monster itself did not know.
Before the final battle, the monster poured most of its energy not into building that huge and horrifying castle, but into rebuilding the 'Sword Garden'.
The monster had put a boundary on the entire restored Sword Garden and built a castle on it.
And all the surviving clansmen were trapped inside, never corrupted.
"He became a monster, and with his power, he corrupted most of the clan's knights...... but he preserved some without damaging them."
"Yeah. The monster left the Sword Garden as remembered by human Rosa Runcandel, not the Sword Garden tainted by her."
Jin remembered the last battle at her words.
The white, lonely landscape that was located deepest within the monster.
"...Perhaps, he might have left the last fortress in preparation for his defeat. Because if he died, you would have to lead the remaining people."
Outside was chaotic.
This was because Jet had gone out and informed them that Jin had awakened.
The heavy footsteps of the clan's knights were causing a vibration.
It was preparation to welcome Jin. Gilly opened the wardrobe and took out a coat that Jin had never worn before.
"Master, you should receive the rest of the details later, and it would be best to go out for now."
Jin stared at the coat, which was similar to the knight's uniform but with different embroidery.
'Ten black swords embroidered on the lapel...'
In Runcandel of Chiron, the only one who had that coat before turning nineteen was Luna.
Because it was a coat symbolizing the 'Xiaojiaju' of the Sword House.
Even when Joshua performed his role as a Xiaojiaju externally, Chiron did not allow him to wear this coat.
"...By any chance, has my father returned?"
"The head of the family has not yet returned."
"Then who can permit me to wear that coat? Even if I establish merit, I can't just wear it myself. I'm still the twelfth knight of the family, Gilly."
Instead of answering, Gilly bowed her head quietly. As if to urge him to wear it quickly.
Eventually, after a few seconds of silence, Jin got up from his place, washed up simply, and put on the coat.
As he stepped outside the room, the knights who had been waiting from the corridor followed Jin, raising their swords in salute.
Jin wanted to confirm the face of each of them, but it seemed he needed to go out to the garden first.
All the surviving clansmen of Runcandel were lined up in the garden.
The brothers, Mary and Tona, were at the forefront, holding up the flag of the clan.
It's always different to hear and actually see.
Jin felt moved as he looked at the lined-up knights.
As Jin approached, the knights retreated to either side, raising their swords in salute.
At the end of the line, there were those Jin had not expected at all.
[Have you come, 12th Knight?]
[Finally, you've woken up.]
Alphen and Tasha were the first to speak to Jin.
And the one-armed former family head standing among them had a face that looked very much like Chiron.
[Welcome, great-grandson.]
The one-armed former head of the family, who was rescued in the last battle, spoke with a grin.
He was the 57th head of the Runcandel and Chiron's grandfather.
